name: AI Roadmap Architect
tag: Walks your team from the first business problem to governed AI at scale, one stage at a time.

scenarios.title: Pick the first AI project
scenarios.ask: We have {ideas} AI ideas from {depts} departments. Help us choose where to start.
steps: Intake
Collected {ideas} ideas with owner, problem and expected benefit.
Scorer
Rated each idea on value, feasibility, data readiness and risk.
Filter
Set aside {=round(ideas * (0.5 - data * 0.1))} ideas that need data you do not have yet.
Shortlist
Picked the top {=min(3, max(1, round(ideas * (0.15 + data * 0.1))))} that can show results in under 90 days.
followups: Problem selection, pilot, production, scale and governance. The tool keeps a checklist for each and only marks a stage done when its checks pass.
Why not start with the biggest idea?
Big ideas usually need more data and change. A quick, visible win builds trust and funding for the bigger ones.

scenarios.title: Plan a pilot
scenarios.ask: Plan a {weeks}-week pilot for invoice matching with {users} users.
steps: Goal setter
Defined success: 80% of invoices matched with no edits, measured weekly.
Planner
Split {weeks} weeks into setup, shadow mode and live use.
Risk check
Listed 4 risks, including vendor names that change format.
Comms
Drafted a kickoff note and a weekly update template for {users} users.
followups: The AI suggests matches but people still do the work as usual. You compare the two before trusting the AI with real decisions.
What if we miss the target?
The plan includes a review at the end. Missing the target is a result too, and the tool records what you learned before the next idea.

scenarios.title: Set up governance at scale
scenarios.ask: We now run {systems} AI systems. Set up governance with a {cadence} review cycle.
steps: Inventory
Listed {systems} systems with owner, data used and decisions they affect.
Risk tiers
Rated {=max(1, round(systems * 0.2))} as high risk because they affect customers or money.
Policy
Drafted rules for testing, human review and incident reporting per tier.
Calendar
Scheduled reviews {cadence} for high-risk systems and yearly for the rest.
followups: It gives a structure that maps to common frameworks. Your legal team should confirm what applies to you.
Every system must have a named business owner and a technical owner before it can be marked compliant.
